title: Setting up
summary: How to sit, how to hold your hands, and how to find your way around the keys.

lessons.title: Sitting and hand shape
lessons.summary: A comfortable position you can keep without strain.

blocks.text: Good technique starts before you play a note. The aim is simple: nothing should feel tight or held. If something hurts while you play, stop and rest.
The app listens to which keys you press, how hard and when. It cannot see your hands, so the points in this lesson are for you to check yourself.

items: Sit on the front half of the bench, feet flat on the floor.
Sit far enough back that your elbows are slightly in front of your body, not pinned to your sides.
Adjust the bench height so your forearms are about level with the keys.
Let your shoulders drop. Check them again after a minute of playing.
Let your fingers curve naturally, as if holding a small ball. The thumb rests on its side corner.
Keep the wrist level with the hand: not sagging below the keys and not arched high.
blocks.text: Check each point at your piano:
Play from the weight of your arm rather than by pressing hard with the fingers alone. A relaxed arm gives a fuller sound for less effort.

exercise.prompt: Something starts to ache in your forearm during practice. What should you do?
options: Push through; it will loosen up
Stop, rest, and check your position before continuing
Lower the bench as far as it goes
exercise.explanation: Pain is a signal to stop. Rest, then check your seat height, shoulders and wrists. If it keeps happening, ask a teacher or a doctor.

blocks.text: The app cannot check any of this for you. Recording a short video of yourself from the side, or a single lesson with a teacher, is the best way to check your position.

lessons.title: Finding your way around the keys
lessons.summary: Use the black keys as landmarks.

blocks.text: The black keys come in groups of two and three. Every C sits just left of a group of two black keys, and every F sits just left of a group of three.
Middle C, and the F above it.
From one key to the very next key, black or white, is a half step. Two half steps make a whole step.
C to C♯ is a half step. C to D is a whole step.

exercise.prompt: Which white key sits just left of a group of three black keys?
exercise.explanation: F is left of the three black keys; C is left of the two.

exercise.prompt: How many half steps are there from E up to F?
exercise.explanation: E and F are next-door white keys with no black key between them: one half step.

exercise.prompt: Play the note a whole step above D4 (the D next to middle C).
exercise.explanation: A whole step above D is E.

exercise.prompt: Play the note a half step above E4.
exercise.explanation: A half step above E is F.
